data.raw_text:
#LATEST After #TyphoonKalmaegi swept across the Philippines, communities in Talisay and Liloan in the province of Cebu were seen left buried in mud and debris on Wednesday. Streets turned into rivers of silt, cars were overturned and houses partially collapsed. Residents waded through thick mud to salvage what remained of their homes, cleaning up broken furniture as well as thick mud from the yards.

Philippine officials said on Wednesday the death toll from the widespread flooding and devastation caused by Typhoon Kalmaegi in the country's central region has risen to at least 114, with 127 others reported missing, many of them in a hard-hit province still recovering from a deadly earthquake.

Kalmaegi made landfall on Tuesday with torrential rains and powerful winds, which caused flooding in several parts of the archipelago especially in Cebu and Leyte. So far rescue and relief efforts have started pouring into affected areas of the country. It is the 20th typhoon to hit the Southeast Asian nation this year amid worsening global climate change.

Typhoon Kalmaegi killed at least 140 people and left another 127 missing after unleashing devastating flooding across the central Philippines, official figures showed Thursday, as the storm headed towards Vietnam.

Floodwaters described as unprecedented rushed through Cebu province's towns and cities this week, sweeping away cars, riverside shanties and even massive shipping containers.

TROPICS: Very sad news, parts of the Philippines, where the death toll from Typhoon Kalmaegi has climbed to 110+

Entire neighborhoods swept away and children, parents, families, their lives changed forever. Over 400,000 people reportedly are displaces after the worst flooding in a very long time there.

Typhoon Kalmaegi is now a Category 4 storm and is forecast to hit Vietnam in the next day or so -- if it does it landfall as a Cat. 4 it will be the strongest typhoon to ever hit Vietnam on record. Quy Nhon & Tuy Hoa could especially get slammed with storm surge and major winds.

The extreme tropical moisture will then flood parts of Laos, eastern Cambodia, and eastern Thailand later this week.
